# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍 ✌ 👎 🤟 ✋]

I need to think about this carefully. I'm the Deaf monkey - I can see the bomb but can't hear speech. Mute just gestured to me, and since I can see gestures, I received them.

Let me analyze what I see on the bomb:
- DISPLAY: 0
- LIGHT: red
- WIRES: 1=red, 2=yellow, 3=green

Mute sent me gestures: [☝ 👍 ✌ 👎 🤟 ✋]

This looks like it could be encoding information from the manual - perhaps mapping to wire numbers or actions. Since gestures have no inherent meaning until we establish one, I should try to interpret this as possibly: ☝(1) 👍(good/yes) ✌(2) 👎(bad/no) 🤟(3) ✋(stop/wait?)

This could mean "wire 1 = good, wire 2 = bad, wire 3 = ?" or similar. But I can't be sure of Mute's intended mapping yet. I need to relay what I see to both Mute and Blind, since Blind cannot see the bomb and needs my description via speech (Blind can hear me), and Mute needs it via speech too since Mute can hear.

Wait - checking the table again: Mute "cannot speak" - so Mute cannot hear either? Let me recheck: Mute's row only specifies what Mute can/cannot do - "Read manual" / "Cannot speak or touch bomb". It doesn't say Mute can't hear. So Mute CAN hear.

I should speak (heard by Mute and Blind) describing the bomb, and watch for Mute's gesture responses to interpret their meaning over time.

```
speak(text="I see: display shows 0, the light is red, and the wires are wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Mute previously sent me a long gesture sequence, and now just sent a single [☝] gesture. This is likely Mute pointing at "wire 1" or emphasizing something specific - possibly confirming or asking about wire 1 specifically, given ☝ often could mean "one" or "first."

Since I can't hear Blind or Mute's speech from previous turns, I don't know what's already been discussed. But my job is to relay bomb details and respond to Mute's gestures with more bomb info, since gestures are likely Mute trying to ask me something about the bomb using a simple numeric code (☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3 could be wire numbers).

Given ☝ alone now, Mute might be asking specifically about wire 1's color, or confirming wire 1. Let me respond by speaking clearly about wire 1 to both Mute and Blind, since that's likely the focus.

```
speak(text="Wire 1 is red, same color as the light. Display still reads 0.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝]

Mute gestured [👍 ☝] - this could mean "yes, wire 1" or "good, one" - possibly confirming that wire 1 (red) is the correct/safe wire to cut, or asking me to confirm again. 

Since I don't hear any speech (from Blind, who might be relaying instructions from Mute since Mute can't touch the bomb), I need to keep providing clear bomb state info and try to establish a gesture-based confirmation loop with Mute.

Let me respond confirming wire 1 is red, and also mention the full state again in case Blind needs it relayed through my speech (Blind can hear me).

```
speak(text="Confirming: wire 1 is red. Display 0, light red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green. Nothing has changed.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 ☝ 👍]

Mute gestured [👉 ☝ 👍] - "👉" could mean "point to" or "you" or "do this", followed by ☝ (one/wire1) and 👍 (yes/good/confirm). This seems like Mute is trying to instruct action on wire 1, but Mute can't touch the bomb either - only Blind can act.

This gesture sequence is likely not meant for me to act on, but rather Mute confirming to me (or through me) that wire 1 is the target action, expecting me to relay this via speech to Blind since Blind can hear me but not see gestures.

Let me relay this interpretation to Blind clearly via speech, along with the bomb state, since Blind needs my spoken description plus whatever Mute has told them.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has gestured toward wire 1 three times now, each time with a thumbs up. I believe Mute is confirming wire 1, which is red, is correct. Display still 0, light red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new gestures from Mute this round - meaning Mute either spoke to Blind directly (which I wouldn't see) or did nothing visible. Since Blind can hear Mute's speech, they may be coordinating directly now without needing gestures to me.

I should stay alert and keep confirming the bomb's current state hasn't changed, in case Blind needs reassurance or in case my last message wasn't fully clear. I'll wait to see if Mute sends me new gestures, but also proactively remind Blind the state is unchanged in case that helps confirm timing before any action.

```
speak(text="No changes: display 0, light red, wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green.")
```
